children: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after metals prices slumped due to soft demand out of China and strengthening bets on Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.

As reported by CNBC, the materials sector faced widespread selling pressure as commodities pulled back sharply across global markets. Industrial and precious metals suffered notable declines, highlighted by spot silver dropping roughly 4% to fall under $47 an ounce and reaching fresh intraday lows. Investors grew cautious as expectations of higher borrowing costs from the Federal Reserve gained momentum, which typically strengthens the dollar and dampens appetite for commodities. Adding to the sector's headwinds, sluggish economic activity and soft consumption in China, the world's largest consumer of raw metals, dampened the demand outlook for producers.
Compounding these macroeconomic pressures, uncertainty around artificial intelligence further weighed on broader investor sentiment, prompting traders to pull back from resource-heavy equities.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:
Metallurgical coal mining company Alpha Metallurgical Resources fell 6.1%.
Precious metals mining company Coeur Mining fell 5.5%.
Precious metals mining company Hecla Mining Company fell 5.7%.
Zooming in on Alpha Metallurgical Resources

Alpha Metallurgical Resources’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 35 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

Alpha Metallurgical Resources is down 29.3% since the beginning of the year, and at $143.61 per share, it is trading 42.5% below its 52-week high of $249.65 from January 2026. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Alpha Metallurgical Resources’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $2,846.
